Architecture

Multiplayer ownership and framework roles

Persistent facts have one durability owner and a current authority session; replication is a projection, not storage.

On this page
Framework placementPersistent fact tableNo client-owned truthReplication lifecycle

Framework placement

Framework objectOwnsMust not own
GameInstance / subsystemsPer-process configuration, local auth session, read-only catalog cachesOther processes’ character truth or shared world ledger
GameModeServer world admission/spawn/rules and ready gateA global cross-zone character database
PlayerControllerConnection ownership, input routing, local UI lifecycleClient-side damage/reward completion
Character/PawnCurrent physical body, movement, live action, cosmetic sprite bridgePermanent player identity through cross-server travel
PlayerStateIn-zone replicated identity, current character projection, player ASCDurability or indefinite cross-server survival
GameStateZone identity, world clock/weather and safe public statePrivate inventory/auth tokens
ActorComponentOne scoped rule/presentation responsibility on explicit ownerAn extra hidden global inventory or duplicate movement clock
Replicated subobjectDeliberately registered compact runtime projection when justifiedAutomatic persistence or assumed Iris compatibility
Zone runtime managerBounded spawn/resource/instance life cycle under one world authorityAn unbounded catch-all manager
Backend service/modelAuthenticated commands, constraints, durable records, session fencingRendering or trusting client-supplied rolls

Persistent fact table

ownership.html is generated from sources/ownership-records.json. Every row names authoritative owner, runtime cache, replication, store, stable key, changes, validation, revision, reconnect policy and UI observer. Database pages describe separate durable models. Model names do not create extra network services.

No client-owned truth

A client may predict motion or a harmless swing visual. It may not decide hit success, node ownership, fish bite, price, item affix, quest completion or final balance. Owner-only state means visible to that owning client, not authoritatively writable by it. A hostile client can change its UI text; the server ignores the forged display.

Replication lifecycle

Bind delegates after both possession and PlayerState readiness. OnRep-style handlers update projections on receipt; they must not reissue durable grants. Late joiners need current property state, not reliance on a past multicast event. Destroyed/recreated bodies reset transient references and rebuild appearance/action from accepted state.
